nativeAxes.front: +X points north-northeast along the leg axis, about17°east of north; +Z points east-southeast; ports face the east-southeast and west-northwest sides
nativeAxes.origin: Ground-level midpoint between the two leg centroids

sourceFacts.reviewScope: Complete static medium-fi exterior of the Gateway Arch itself: NPS weighted catenary, equilateral triangular taper, both ground-clipped steel feet, three outer faces,32 recessed observation ports and low crown service hatch. The unchanged50314triangle detailed source master remains reproducible. Skyline is a complete128-segment catenary with triangular faces; district retains all32 actual port holes/reveals and street adds simplified shop and field welds; closeup retains the full detailed geometry. Weld station locations, port station offsets and service-hatch sizes remain photographic reconstructions. NPS fact-sheet27inch port width and HSR approximate24inch clear width differ and remain explicitly recorded. The two below-grade leg exit courts, visitor/museum building, underground interior, ramps and wider landscaped park are separate site architecture outside this steel-arch asset. GroundY0 is the upper steel-foot contact datum, not the lower exit court. Four mapped outer-foot corners constrain a rigid rotation/translation with no scaling; maximum residual below3m and2° heading tolerance acknowledge map generalization. OSM relation12813920 incorrectly carries the park Q45234; identity uses exactQ2027162 node4004558403, supported by the named steel-arch relation and observed feet. Common brushed-stainless graph approximates finish; local oil-canning, staining and individual weld condition are not duplicated. Absolute site elevation, live host terrain and physical phone/laptop timings remain unmeasured.
